episodes.178430: Showers around an upper-level low produced several gale-force wind gusts.
episodes.178480: A coastal California Low along with ridging across the intermountain west, produced areas of gusty winds to start the month of May.
episodes.178573: Accelerated snowmelt from a near-record snowpack due to above normal temperatures produced high and fast flow on drainages in portions of San Miguel and Mesa counties. As a result, flooding and debris flows compromised Fall Creek Road as well as portions of the Riverfront Trail along the Colorado River in Grand Junction.
episodes.179186: Snowmelt from warming temperatures combined with a multiple day moderate to heavy rain event pushed some area streams and creeks out of their banks.
episodes.179205: A weak shortwave trough, combined with favorable instability and marginally supportive wind shear, lead to the development of strong thunderstorms across portions of western-north Texas. Small hail was observed with a thunderstorm in Wichita County.
episodes.179239: Snowmelt and rainfall created a steady rise for the Clark Fork River above Missoula. River levels exceeded minor flood stage, and remained there over the course of a week.
episodes.180624: A negatively-tilted, shortwave trough across the Four Corners brought lee troughing across the Southern Plains. A dryline was positioned across portions of west Texas and southeast New Mexico. Many splitting supercells developed along the dryline, producing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180626: A negatively-tilted, shortwave trough across the Four Corners brought lee troughing across the Southern Plains. A dryline was positioned across portions of west Texas and southeast New Mexico. Many splitting supercells developed along the dryline, producing large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180627: Continued lee troughing resulting from a large-scale upper-low across the western CONUS brought additional thunderstorms to the area. Afternoon and evening thunderstorms formed along the higher elevations and tracked eastward producing reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180628: Continued lee troughing resulting from a large-scale upper-low across the western CONUS brought additional thunderstorms to the area. Afternoon and evening thunderstorms formed along the higher elevations and tracked eastward producing reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.180759: Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay and Virginia Coastal Waters.
episodes.180760: Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.180832: An isolated storm produced small hail across Stanton County.
episodes.180898: The combination of weak upper level disturbances and moderate instability resulted in isolated severe thunderstorms mainly across portions of the Heartland during the afternoon and evening hours. The severe storms produced large hail and a few damaging wind reports.
episodes.181052: A slow moving Low brought slow moving thunderstorms with hail, wind, and heavy rain. The heavy rains and snow melt caused flooding issues and washouts.
episodes.181055: A slow moving Low brought several rounds of thunderstorms, heavy rain, and flooding from snow melt across North Idaho.
episodes.181187: Near record snowpack began melting out during the month of May and brought widespread minor flooding to the Bear River in Lincoln County.

Increased flood waters due to rapid snowmelt led to water and debris across Fall Creek Road from County Road 56L to the Little Cone Ranch Subdivision. The road was closed for several hours.

Minor flooding occurred along Landing Road, near Elk River. Flowing water came out of the banks of Elk Creek and covered some roadways. The main impact areas were rural and recreational, including near an RV park. Water damaged parts of the road, as confirmed by social media pictures.

The Clark Fork River above Missoula reached minor flood stage of 7.5 feet by 1100MST on May 3rd. The river remained above minor flood stage through 1900MST on May 11th. The river crested at 9.5 feet around 0400MST on May 7th. This did cause sandbagging efforts in the frequently flooded area of Tower and Kehrwald streets in the Orchard Homes neighborhood of Missoula.

Minor flooding occurred in southern Lincoln County, with the most affected area along the Bear River near Pixley Dam. The floods were largely confined to low-lying agricultural land and a few dirt roads near the river. This first flood wave from melt in the lower and mid elevations was the highest peak of the season, with peak flow at the Bear River below Pixley Dam gauge reading of 1760 CFS.
